title: India's Evolving Legal Landscape: Demystifying the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act 2026
content:
# India's Evolving Legal Landscape: Demystifying the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act 2026

Namaste, fellow professionals! The legislative wheels in India are always turning, aren't they? Just when you think you've got a handle on the existing framework, a new Act arrives, promising to reshape aspects of our intricate legal and fiscal environment. The latest entrant to this dynamic arena is the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026**, which received Presidential assent on August 17, 2026. This isn't just another routine amendment; it brings about some targeted yet significant changes across direct taxation, digital payments, and incentives for crucial sectors. It's time to roll up our sleeves and delve into the nuances, because *yeh changes toh humein samajhne hi padenge* to advise our clients effectively.

The Act primarily amends the **Income Tax Act, 2025** (which, as you know, recently replaced the venerable Income Tax Act, 1961), the **Finance Act, 2026**, and notably, the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**. The underlying objectives appear to be multi-faceted: attracting foreign capital, promoting domestic manufacturing, simplifying compliance, and providing greater clarity in specific tax areas. Let's break down the key amendments.

## Digital Payment Flexibility: Amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007

In our increasingly digital economy, the government's push for electronic transactions is clear. This Act streamlines the regulatory process for prescribing electronic payment modes. Earlier, the ability to specify electronic payment methods was tied to a specific section of the erstwhile Income Tax Act. The new amendment decouples this, granting more flexibility to tax authorities.

### The Shift in Specifying Electronic Payment Modes

| **Old Provision (Section 10A, PSS Act, 2007, prior to amendment)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **New Provision (Post-amendment to Section 10A, PSS Act, 2007)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Section 10A referred to electronic payment modes *prescribed under Section 269SU of the Income Tax Act, 1961*. This created a direct linkage to a specific, now repealed, provision of the old tax law.                                                                                                                                | The amendment replaces this reference, allowing the Central Government to specify one or more electronic modes of payment by notification *under Section 187 of the Income Tax Act, 2025*. This enables tax authorities to prescribe payment methods without direct linkage to a former Income Tax Act section.                                     |

**Implications:** This is a forward-looking change. By shifting the power to Section 187 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, the government ensures that the framework for digital payments remains adaptable and can evolve with technological advancements and policy objectives without needing to amend the PSS Act repeatedly. It signifies greater autonomy for tax authorities in promoting digital transactions, *jo ki aaj ke time mein bahut zaroori hai*.

## Boosting Foreign Investment: Revamped Framework for FIIs and Fund Managers

India's ambition to become a global investment hub is evident in the strategic tax reliefs offered to foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and measures to ease the relocation of fund managers. The Act introduces targeted changes to support international investment.

### Simplified Conditions and New Exemptions

| **Old Provision (Under Income Tax Act, 2025 and earlier laws)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **New Provision (Post-amendment)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Safe Harbour for Fund Managers:** Required meeting a longer list of conditions to ensure that a fund manager's global income would not be taxed in India, often posing a compliance challenge.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The Act makes it easier for fund managers to relocate to India by significantly cutting down on the list of conditions that these funds must satisfy for their global income to avoid being taxed in India. This rationalizes conditions for eligible investment funds and fund managers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Taxation of Income from Government Securities for FIIs/BIS:** Interest income was taxed at 20%, short-term capital gains at 30%, and long-term capital gains at 12.5% for FIIs and the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) on investments in Indian government securities.                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The Act introduces new exemptions under Schedule IV of the Income Tax Act 2025 for specified recipients earning income from Indian government securities. It exempts FIIs and the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) from income tax on interest earned from investments in government securities and capital gains arising from their sale, exchange, or transfer. This exemption applies to income arising on or after April 1, 2026.                                                                    |

**Implications:** *Yeh toh seedha-seedha foreign capital ko bulane ka tareeka hai!* By simplifying the 'safe harbour' provisions and exempting income from government securities, India is sending a clear signal to global investors and fund managers: we want your business, and we're making it easier for you. This move is expected to enhance liquidity in the government securities market and attract more foreign portfolio investment.

## 'Make in India' and Electronics Manufacturing: Extended Incentives

The government's steadfast commitment to boosting domestic manufacturing, particularly in the electronics sector, finds renewed emphasis in this Act. The aim is to provide policy certainty and encourage greater investment in this high-growth area.

### Tax Holidays and Component Storage Exemptions

| **Old Provision (Under Income Tax Act, 2025 and earlier laws)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **New Provision (Post-amendment)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Contract Manufacturing Exemption:** Income tax exemptions were available to foreign companies engaging contract manufacturers in India for producing electronic goods, but the sunset clause was nearing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The Act extends the income tax exemption for foreign companies that engage a contract manufacturer in India for producing specified electronic goods until the tax year ending March 31, 2041 (i.e., till 2040-41). Specified electronic goods include mobile phones, laptops, servers, and their sub-assemblies. This provides long-term policy certainty to the sector.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Components in Bonded Warehouses:** Previously, there might have been ambiguity or tax implications on the sale of components stored in customs bonded areas by foreign companies to their Indian contract manufacturers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | A new exemption has been introduced for income arising to a foreign company on the sale of components stored in a warehouse within a customs bonded area, provided these components are supplied to a contract manufacturer for use in producing specified electronic goods. This exemption lasts for 15 years, to the tax year ending March 31, 2041. This measure complements the capital goods exemption and covers the components that foreign companies sell to contract manufacturers for finished goods. This applies to income arising on or after October 1, 2026. |

**Implications:** This is a huge shot in the arm for the "Make in India" initiative, particularly in electronics. Extending the tax holiday period till 2041 provides significant long-term certainty, encouraging foreign players to establish and expand their manufacturing footprint here. The exemption for components stored in bonded warehouses is a practical step, reducing an potential logistical and tax hurdle. *Ab toh electronic goods banana aur bhi aasaan ho jayega India mein!*

## Refined Definitions for Data Centres and SPVs: Clarity in Taxation

The Act also brings clarity to the taxation landscape for specific business structures like data centres and Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) of business trusts, recognizing their growing importance in the modern economy.

### Defining Eligibility and Differentiating Tax Treatment

| **Old Provision (Under Income Tax Act, 2025 and Finance Act, 2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | **New Provision (Post-amendment)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Specified Data Centres:** The definition of "specified data centre" under Schedule IV of the Income Tax Act 2025 might have lacked precise criteria.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The Act amends the definition of a "specified data centre" under Schedule IV of the Income Tax Act 2025. Under the amended definition, a specified data centre must meet two conditions: an Indian company must operate it (either by owning or leasing), and it must satisfy any other conditions prescribed under the applicable rules. This provides simplified conditions for the data centre services exemption.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Tax Rates for SPVs of Domestic Companies:** The Finance Act, 2026, might have had a uniform approach to domestic company taxation or specific surcharge rates that didn't differentiate for SPVs of business trusts opting for concessional regimes.                                                                                                                                                                | The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act 2026 introduces separate tax rates for domestic companies based on whether they qualify as specified Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). Furthermore, for SPVs of business trusts (like REITs and InvITs) that opt into a concessional tax regime, the surcharge rate on income tax payable has been *raised to 25%* (from 10% under Finance Act, 2026). This aims to balance incentives with revenue considerations for these pass-through vehicles. The dividend exemption for unit holders is now extended even if the SPV opts for the new tax regime. |

**Implications:** Clarifying the definition of data centres is crucial for the booming digital infrastructure sector, enabling them to avail intended tax benefits. For SPVs, the differentiated tax rates and increased surcharge for those opting for concessional regimes reflect a nuanced approach to taxing business trusts. Professionals need to carefully analyze the structure of SPVs and their chosen tax regimes to ensure optimal compliance and planning.

## Strategic Relief for Diamond Trading: A Gem in the Amendments

Recognizing India's prominence in the global diamond trade, the Act provides a specific tax exemption aimed at enhancing the ease of doing business for foreign players in this sector.

### New Exemption for Rough Diamond Mining Companies

| **Old Provision (Under Income Tax Act, 2025)**                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **New Provision (Post-amendment)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Income generated from the sale of rough diamonds in India by foreign companies was subject to standard income tax provisions, potentially impacting their operational model or profitability in India.                                              | The Act introduces a new exemption for foreign rough diamond mining companies. Income from the sale of rough diamonds in a notified special zone will be exempt. This applies to foreign companies engaged in diamond mining or sightholders of such companies, as well as brokers, aggregators, or tender and auction entities connected with the sale of rough diamonds. This exemption applies to income arising on or after October 1, 2026, and will be available until March 31, 2041. |

**Implications:** This is a strategic move to boost India's position as a global diamond trading hub. By providing a direct tax exemption, the government is incentivizing foreign diamond mining and trading companies to route their sales through India, bringing more business and potentially creating more jobs in the sector. *Yeh toh diamond industry ke liye ek chamakta hua decision hai!*

## Final Thoughts

The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, with its Presidential assent on August 17, 2026, is a testament to India's continuous effort to adapt its legal and fiscal framework to evolving economic realities and global trends. From fostering digital payments to energizing domestic manufacturing, attracting foreign investment, and streamlining sector-specific tax treatments, this Act presents a blend of strategic reliefs and clarifications.

For us, as Chartered Accountants and Legal Analysts, understanding these amendments is not just about compliance; it's about identifying opportunities and navigating potential challenges for our clients. The changes reflect a proactive approach by the government to create a more investment-friendly and digitally-forward economy. We must stay vigilant, analyze the detailed rules and notifications that will follow, and accordingly advise businesses to leverage these new provisions effectively. It’s an exciting time to be in practice, *hai na*?
